correctness.rationale: The forward subsets satisfying the degree condition are matchings, and either reversed arc can be added without a cycle. With both additions, a cycle is possible exactly when both cross edges are chosen, since consecutive forward arcs are impossible and the two reversed arcs have disjoint endpoints. If cross-completeness fails, the full simplicial join with the edge on the reversed arcs is a cone. Otherwise let C be the join of that edge with the forward matchings avoiding the cross pair, and K the residual matching complex. The full multipath complex is C union (∂Δ³ * K), where Δ³ has the four special arcs as vertices. Their intersection is the join of the edge on the reversed arcs, the boundary of the edge on the cross arcs, and K, hence is contractible. The intersection inclusions are simplicial cofibrations, so the inclusion ∂Δ³ * K into the union gives the claimed equivalence. This also gives S² directly when K consists only of the empty face. Threefold integral homology shift and Jonsson's exact chessboard group yield the stated K7,7 corollary. The frozen checker and verification prose were inspected without executing the checker; mod-two runs cannot substantiate integral torsion.
